summary:
I wrote plan.md for the Capitol. It runs north to south and mirrors exactly about z 47.5: Senate wing (z 2..18), connector, central block (x 10..29), connector, House wing (z 77..93). All balustrades sit at y 12, with arcaded rusticated basements, long west colonnades, pedimented east porticos, an arcaded West Front with double flights of steps, and a staggered double-row East Portico.
The dome is laid out on even-diameter rings around x 20, z 48 and climbs to y 41: square base, a 16-wide peristyle of about 24 columns with a lit drum behind, a 14-wide attic, a 12-wide bell shell with 8 grey ribs, a 4-wide lantern, and a dark Statue of Freedom on top. That puts the dome about 3x the wing height, as on the real building.
The palette is white quartz, calcite and diorite with teal copper cupolas; the lit drum, lantern and skylights glow warm at dusk. Unchecked: nothing has been built or rendered, and the broad east steps fall outside the plot. White neoclassical Capitol symmetric about z 47.5: two balustraded wings with west colonnades and east pedimented porticoes, a central block with the West Front loggia and East Portico, and the stepped peristyle, ribbed bell dome, tholos and bronze Freedom statue (y41) on the d16/d12/d4 rings.
Exterior-only solid core (spawn-proof), warm glowstone and lanterns at the base and in the drum, lantern and skylights for dusk. elements.md and plan.md (PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS, PARTS) are written; all block ids are 1.21.1-valid.

Masonry shell: parts/shell.mjs builds the masonry shell. That covers rusticated podiums to ground, 2-thick walls y5..11 on both wings, connectors, central block and antae, smooth_stone core, decks y12, West Front arcade podium and deck, terrace plinths, and the N/S west steps.
Window, door, arch, column, pediment, dome, cupola and skylight cells are left unset rather than set to air, so later parts can fill them.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no refused or off-palette writes. The render shows the shell sitting where the plan puts it. check reports 0 floating blocks and 6 harmless orphans at the lintel gaps. I did not run `mcd fit`.
polish: Not built, left to P2: entablature y11 and cornices over the loggias, the loggia ceiling and deck at x3..5 y12, and the sill band at y5.
The glow cell behind every window is unset. P5 should fill it with glowstone where lit and smooth_stone elsewhere, or leave 1x1x2 air pockets that could spawn mobs.
Terrace plinths are a brick course plus a bottom slab at G+1, so they sit 1.5 blocks above the ground; P6 may need a slab ramp.
The West Front loggia x8..9 and the wing loggias x3..4 are open and unroofed until P2 adds the entablature.
Wing podium strip and wing east podium (x34..35) are built; the portico floor slab at y5 is P2's.

waste.what: Enumerated every window/door/arch/reserved cell by hand into a reserved set so openings stay unset, because wingBody and podium fill over those cells and have no skip parameter
waste.cost: about 40 lines of coordinates, one pass
waste.tool: wingBody/podium helpers that accept a `reserve`/`skip(x,y,z)` predicate, plus a shared openings table (plan OPENINGS as data) used by both shell and fittings

waste.what: Mirrored the House wing windows and arches by hand (z to 95-z, facing flip)
waste.cost: small
waste.tool: a mirrorZ-aware opening-table helper

companions.task: Quoins, the sill band and the slab cornices at the podium top and y11
Check that the west steps meet the loggia floor and the terrace kit without a full-block jump

summary:
Colonnades, porticoes, pediments, balustrades, cupolas: parts/colonnades.mjs builds the wing colonnades (Senate and House, x3 with corner piers), both wing east porticoes with pediments, the West Front loggia columns and entablature, the East Portico (staggered columns, bottom-slab floor, entablature, pediment), y12 balustrades on the wing, connector and central rooflines, the N/S copper cupolas and the two chamber skylights.
make.sh ran clean: my part placed 1634 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; fit is OK; check shows no floating groups. Front-left/right renders and zooms of the West loggia and East Portico read as intended.
Not done here: the West Front arcade and terrace balustrade (P5/P6), the East Portico bronze door (P5), the proud-1 cornice course on the entablatures, and the chiseled tympanum was only checked by eye.
polish: Elements 8 (West Front) is only partly mine: the loggia columns, entablature and x8 balustrade are built; the arcade podium with its 7 arches, the upper terrace deck and the x0 balustrade belong to P5/P6.
Element 10: the double bronze door at x29 z47..48 is P5's and not built here; the columns, floor, entablature and pediment are done.
Element 12 (entablature cornice proud 1, smooth_quartz_slab top) is not built; I laid only the smooth_quartz y11 band.
The pediment tympanum and rakes were checked by eye at zoom, not measured against the plan's stair and chiseled-block positions.
Shell (P1) leaves 6 orphan smooth_quartz blocks (x5 y8 z3/z17/z78/z92, x33 y8 z16/z79); they are not mine but the check flags them.
plan.md has no checklist; I ticked elements 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15 in elements.md instead.

waste.what: Mirrored every Senate-side coordinate by hand for the House side (z -> 95 - z) and wrote the mirror logic for balustrade lines myself.
waste.cost: About 15 coordinate lists and a mirrorLine helper worked out by hand; one bug (a floor loop that would overwrite column cells) found on review.
waste.tool: A mirror helper in the vocab (or the build library's mirrorZ at cz 47.5) that takes one Senate-side call list and writes the House copy, plus a balustrade-lines-from-wall-outline helper.

waste.what: Per-cell loops for the portico floor, the entablature fills and the skylight curb and glass rectangle.
waste.cost: About 6 nested loops and roughly 400 g.set calls written by hand across the part.
waste.tool: A portico helper that takes the floor cells, the column cells and the entablature in one call (the vocab portico exists, but its floor and column cells overlap at y5 and it has no way to skip column cells), and a skylight(curb, glass, glow) helper.

waste.what: Visual checks by render and zoom, one at a time.
waste.cost: 3 renders and zooms (front-left, front-right, East Portico, West loggia), read by eye.
waste.tool: mcd card --layout eye or a per-element pass that checks a named cell list, instead of reading tiles by eye.

companions.task: Lay the entablature bands, the balustrade caps and the portico floor slabs, so the wing and portico tops read as dressed stone rather than flat fills.
Set the skylight glass panes at y13 and the curb ring at y12 so the glazing lines up with the roof and the glow below.
Cut the pediment raking stairs (the tympanum courses) to the 1-up-per-2-across pitch and check the chiseled centre block.

summary:
Dome lower: Dome lower is built in parts/dome-lower.mjs: the 18x18 smooth_quartz base with a top-slab cornice at y14, a d16 peristyle of 24 quartz_pillar columns y15..20 around a lit calcite d12 drum (glowstone behind each window, smooth_stone core inside, standing lanterns), a full smooth_quartz disc at y21 with a diorite_wall ring at y22, and the attic (d14 ring y22..24 with windows at y23, smooth_stone core, cornice disc y25).
Verified: make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt, Dome lower placed 2658 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; `mcd fit` is OK; `mcd check` reports nothing in my cells (its 6 orphans are at x5/x33 z3..92, y8, from P1's shell); zoomed render from west and north shows the columns, lit drum, balustrade ring and attic.
Ticked elements.md 16, 17, 18 and added a P3 note to plan.md.
polish: Entablature cornice: the outer ring of the y21 disc has no smooth_quartz_slab cornice (a plain full disc instead).
Balustrade posts: the y22 ring is diorite_wall on every d16 cell; the smooth_quartz posts every 6th cell from the plan are not placed.
Light not measured on the peristyle floor: `mcd light` needs room boxes (rooms.json is empty), so only the lantern placement was checked by reading the helper, not the light map.
P1 shell leaves 6 orphan smooth_quartz blocks at x5 and x33 (y8, z3/17/16/78/79/92); `mcd check` flags them, they are not in this part.
Dome shell (P4) not built here; it starts on the y25 cornice disc that this part leaves in place.

waste.what: Re-derived the d12 drum interior by hand: a kept() formula copied from the vocab, plus a 4-neighbour loop to find interior cells, then an air-only smooth_stone fill.
waste.cost: about 15 lines of coordinate code and one retry
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as solidCore(g, {cx, cz, d, y0, y1, block, over}) or an exported kept(d, cx, cz) and ringOf(), so the core fill and the ring tests are not rewritten.

waste.what: Checked the balustrade and post spacing by eye: ringPost gives one block everywhere and the plan wants smooth_quartz posts every 6th cell, so I had to read ringPost and wallState to see what it would write.
waste.cost: 2 source reads and a design decision with no tool support
waste.tool: ringBalustrade(g, {cx, cz, d, y, postEvery, post, rail}) in vocab/h3, which would write the rail and the posts at once like balustrade() does for straight lines.

waste.what: Verified the peristyle lantern and standable rules by reading the helper source, not by a check.
waste.cost: one source read
waste.tool: `mcd light` with a room box for the dome floor (the light tool only measures rooms, so an unnamed floor area needs a rooms.json entry).

companions.task: Cut the entablature cornice: a smooth_quartz_slab course on the outer d16 ring at y21 to replace the plain full disc edge, and the projecting cornice line over the peristyle.
Measure the light on the peristyle floor and in the drum interior with a room box for the colonnade, then place a lantern where any cell reads dark (0).

summary:
Dome upper: P4 dome upper built in parts/dome-upper.mjs: ribbed bell shell y26..33 (d12→d4, stepped stair edges, 8 polished_diorite ribs, 8 windows at y27), tholos y34..37 (diorite posts, glowstone core, d4 stair cap, d2 top), and the Statue of Freedom at (19,38..41,47).
Make.sh saved a whole build.nbt: 628 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Shell and tholos are mirror-symmetric about the dome axis (x→39−x, z→95−z); only the statue sits off-centre, by design.
Ticked elements 19, 20 and 21 in elements.md; added a P4 note to plan.md's Notes.
polish: The shell's bottom course (y26 d12) rests on P3's y25 cornice disc; in this isolated build the whole 628-block dome upper is FLOATING until dome-lower lands (the $MCD check reports it). Nothing to change in P4 once P3 is in.

The y33 d4 ring is full smooth_quartz (domeShell's own top course), not the slab-topped ring the plan names. Left as is and noted in plan.md Notes; a slab cap would need a helper change or a local write.

Visual check was done on a throwaway copy with a d14 core stood under the dome (not written to the part): the stepped bell, ribs, windows, lantern and statue read correctly. The whole-building render is the integration check and is not done here.

waste.what: Checked the dome's mirror symmetry with a hand-written script that loops over every cell and compares it with its mirror (x→39−x, z→95−z).
waste.cost: one throwaway script, one run; about 15K tokens of context
waste.tool: A `mcd symmetry build.nbt --axis x=39 --axis z=95 [--box ...]` command (or a mirror option on `$MCD check`) that reports asymmetric cells per box.

waste.what: To see the dome as a whole, I wrote a throwaway script that filled the air under the shell with a d14 core, then zoomed. Nothing in the kit gives a stand-in for a part that is still a stub.
waste.cost: one throwaway script, two renders
waste.tool: A `mcd render --fill-stub` option, or a build.mjs flag that runs the other parts' stand-ins, so a single part can be viewed in place.

waste.what: Read the vocabulary's domeShell, tholos and statue source to confirm the coordinates and that they write only into air.
waste.cost: about 3 greps and one source read
waste.tool: The vocab helper comments could state the footprint and the cells each helper leaves unset, so a worker does not need to read the source.

companions.task: Lay the bell's stepped courses by hand: check the upright stair lips on the d12→d10→d8→d6→d4 edges and the rib joints where the stones meet, against a template of the profile, to confirm the curve reads smooth from the street.

Model the Statue of Freedom figure (a 3-block dark bronze figure with its helmet and shoulders) in the right silhouette: the polished_blackstone and wall blocks are only a rough stand-in for the figure, and this is the one piece the street view sees against the sky.

summary:
Facade fittings: parts/fittings.mjs builds every OPENINGS window (tall with diorite lintels, short, every third lit from behind, unlit glow cells filled with core), the 8 West Front arcade arches, the 16 wing podium arches, and the 4 bronze doors (Senate/House east, West Front, East Portico).
make.sh runs whole: Facade fittings placed 1576 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check, fit and zoom renders look right at the west front and the east wing door.
Pilasters (element 13) and the y11 chiseled panels are not built: their cells are shell wall, and the rule against overwriting locked cells blocks them. plan.md Notes says what the shell must leave open.
polish: Flush pilasters (elements.md 13) and the corner piers' fittings are not placed: pilaster cells are shell wall (smooth_quartz at x5, x33, x10, x29 and the odd z between windows), and writing quartz_pillar over them would overwrite locked blocks. The shell has to leave those cells unset, or the pilasters get a permission to cut, before they can be added.
The y11 chiseled_quartz_block panels at x17..18 on the wing north/south ends (z2 and z93) are not placed for the same reason: y11 there is shell wall.
elements.md 13 stays unticked for that reason. Window glass, lintels and glow are in; the lit-window part of 23 is only the glowstone behind panes, and the lanterns and base glow are P6's.
Pane connection states are set by windowBay, but they were checked only by eye in the zoom, not by a census against the OPENINGS table.

waste.what: Worked out each OPENINGS row by hand (which z or x, both rows or tall only, lit or not), then mirrored the House side by hand (z -> 95 - z and FLIP north/south) and sorted the lists to count the every-third lit rhythm.
waste.cost: about 40 window positions and 8 wall lists, several passes to get the mirror and the sort order right
waste.tool: A windowBay-by-row helper that takes an OPENINGS table row (face, wall, positions, rows, lit rule) and mirrors it, so the House side comes from the Senate's rows with no hand arithmetic.

waste.what: The unlit window's glow cell (two in from the outer face) had to be filled with core by hand after each windowBay call, because windowBay writes nothing there when lit is false. Otherwise it leaves a sealed air pocket in the wall.
waste.cost: one closeCore pass per window row, about 120 cells
waste.tool: windowBay should fill its third cell with the core block when lit is false, or take a core option. It is a one-line change in vocab/h2.mjs.

waste.what: Read shell.mjs's win() to confirm which cells the shell reserved for each window, because the reservation is not exported anywhere a fittings part can read.
waste.cost: one full read of a 7.9 KB source file
waste.tool: The shell should export its reserved-cell list (or the OPENINGS table as data), so fittings can check its cells against it.

waste.what: Checked the windows by zooming, not by a census of glazed panes against the OPENINGS table.
waste.cost: 3 zoom renders and eye review
waste.tool: A census check (for example `$MCD check` with an OPENINGS manifest) that counts gray_stained_glass_pane per row and fails on a missing one.

companions.task: Cut the flush quartz_pillar pilasters and corner piers into the shell walls (odd z on x5, x33, x10 and x29 between the windows) and the chiseled panels at y11 on the north and south ends. These are cuts into a finished wall, so the stonemason would need the shell to open those cells first.
Fill the glow cell behind every third window and check each lit bay reads as a warm lit pane at dusk, with the unlit cells kept as solid core and no air pocket left inside the wall.

Hang the four bronze dark_oak doors and their transoms: double leaves at the West Front (x10 z47..48) and the East Portico (x29 z47..48), single leaves at z10 and z85 on the east wing, with the hinges matched to the leaf.

summary:
Lighting and terrace edges: P6 lighting is built in parts/lighting.mjs: the upper west terrace balustrade with post lamps, north and south terrace lamp lines on their plinths, and hanging loggia and East Portico lanterns, plus 8 standing base lanterns on the podium ledges.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with 65 P6 blocks, 0 refused and 0 off-palette; $MCD check reports 0 floating blocks.
The loggia and portico lanterns only place once the y11 entablature (P2) exists, so I checked their light with a scratch stand-in for it: the East Portico and loggia floors go from 44 dark cells to 0, with the remaining cells at 3-6.
polish: The hanging loggia and East Portico lanterns (x4, x9, x31 at y10) only place once P2 builds the y11 entablature over them; in this copy they are refused and were verified only with a scratch stand-in (/tmp/sim-p6/sim.mjs).
The West Front steps' top-landing lanterns are not placed: the landing top is a bottom slab, which lanterns refuse. Those cells read dim (3-6) on the floor light map, below the 8+ target.
Plan deviation: the upper west terrace balustrade is at y6, not y5, because the shell's y5 deck slab occupies x0; its post lamps stand at y7. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
Roof decks at y12 (open to sky, inside the balustraded lines) have no lamps; the plan gives no lamp positions for them, so they may spawn mobs at night.
elements.md item 23 is not ticked: its glowstone and shroomlight window glow belongs to the fittings and shell parts, and the entablature-dependent lanterns are unverified in the merged build.

waste.what: Wrote the hanging-lantern bay positions (x4 z4,8,12,16 and the mirrors; x9 and x31 z42,46,49,53) and the terrace post positions by hand, and worked out each terrace column's ground-dependent height G+2 and G+3 cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 12 coordinate sets and 2 mirror checks, plus one rebuild.
waste.tool: A vocab helper like lanternRow with every-Nth-bay-centre plus mirror (z -> 95-z) support, and a balustrade variant that takes a per-column y from G(x,z) instead of one y per call.

waste.what: Found the wrong block id by trial: B.wall('diorite_wall') produced diorite_wall_wall, so the palette report refused it on the first build.
waste.cost: 1 failed make.sh run and 1 retry.
waste.tool: A note in the build library's B.wall doc that the argument is the material stem (diorite), not the block id; or a palette check that suggests the stem.

waste.what: Could not test the loggia lanterns in the merged build because the entablature is another part's stub; I wrote a scratch script that stands in for the entablature so the light map could be checked.
waste.cost: 1 scratch script and 3 light-map runs.
waste.tool: mcd light --assume-cells, or a way to run a single part with the earlier parts' stand-ins from plan.md, so a part's light can be checked before the merge.

waste.what: Checked light by reading the floor-level grid by eye instead of against a numeric target per room.
waste.cost: about 6 reads of the full light map.
waste.tool: mcd light --y N --min 8 --list-dark, which prints only the dark or dim cells as coordinates; rooms.json has no exterior rooms, so per-room checks don't apply here.

companions.task: Confirm the north and south terrace plinth courses (bricks at G, slab at G+1) and the balustrade heights at G+2 against the ground steps, so the terrace lamp posts sit on full blocks at every column.

Review the loggia and portico lantern spacing once the entablature exists, and decide whether the west steps' landing needs a hidden light (a glow behind a pane) instead of a lantern that the bottom-slab landing refuses.

summary: inspection: Fixed the 32 fit issues (terrace balustrade and post cells on the bottom-slab plinth at G+1, x10..25 on z0 and z95) by making the plinth's G+1 course two full quartz_bricks courses in parts/shell.mjs; the lighting.mjs comment now matches. ./make.sh rebuilt build.nbt; walk is ok with no rooms and fit reports OK.

waste.what: The fit output printed only 8 of its 32 issues, so I had to infer that the other 24 were the same terrace cells (x10..25 on both z0 and z95) from the plan and code instead of reading them.
waste.cost: One grep plus two file reads to map the 8 listed cells to shell.mjs:108-111.
waste.tool: mcd fit should print every issue, or at least a count per pattern with the first few cells, when it lists 32.

waste.what: The fit message suggests a top slab or full block but does not say which keeps the plan's walkable top. I chose full bricks at G+1, which departs from the plan's bottom-slab top, and worked that out by hand.
waste.cost: One judgement call and a comment update in two files.
waste.tool: The fit line could name the owning code site (here the shell.mjs terrace plinth loop) so the fix location needs no grep.
